headline: Neural mass models and higher-order measures assessed against brain dynamics
label: Model Validation Against Neural Data
summary: Reviews of higher-order information measures and unified neural mass frameworks sharpen how model outputs are tested against neural and speech data.
synthesis: The dominant thread is the use of explicit formal frameworks to constrain mechanistic claims about brain and motor dynamics. A review of higher-order information measures, including synergy, redundancy, and partial information decomposition, examines both the promise and the pitfalls of inferring mechanisms from these quantities in neural and cognitive data. A separate preprint proposes an alternative representation of discrete articulatory movements that reveals pervasive limit-cycle rhythmicity in speech motor activity. A unifying framework orders neural mass models from push-pull oscillators to coupled whole-brain networks, providing a common reference for brain oscillation modelling. What is new is the attempt to place model classes and information measures on a shared footing for comparison with biological data. Validity still depends on which quantities are mapped and what benchmarks they are tested against.
